analysis.file_name: Forget The Retail Trader_ Goldman Says Everything Now Rides On The Top 10%, Who Own 87% Of Household Stocks.pdf
analysis.title: US Weekly Kickstart: One step back from the retail trader, two steps forward from household equity demand
key_insights: Goldman's Ben Snider says household demand is the key support for US equities as hedge funds degross and equity supply rises. Retail trading has declined but total household demand has been very strong this year.

Hedge funds degrossed in 7 of the past 8 sessions. Goldman's Hedge Fund VIP long/short basket pair fell about 4% on Thursday, a move only rivaled in the past decade on DeepSeek Monday (Jan 2025) and the COVID sell-off (Mar 2020). Goldman's Prime desk, using a longer lookback, called it the worst day since 2011.

Goldman Prime Services estimates fundamental hedge fund net leverage is close to 5-year lows, while gross leverage remains above the 90th percentile on a 5-year view. Louis Miller notes that with 90% of Prime book gross in quants and multi-managers, short-term stops matter more than medium-term value.

Retail trading volumes in US equities are down about 20% since the summer and about 45% since late 2025. Retail is 9% of total US equity volume, down from 15% late last year and near the lowest since 2020, despite a modest uptick over the past two weeks.

Goldman attributes the retail decline mainly to weak consumer sentiment and rising energy prices. Economists estimate 2026 real income growth at 1%, with resilient spending sustained partly by a lower personal saving rate.

Some retail activity has moved to leveraged ETFs, where retail share of trading is roughly double that of unlevered ETFs on the same indices. The past two weeks saw a surge of inflows into the 10 biggest levered products as the market fell.

Prediction market volumes reached $78B in September, up from $5B a year earlier. Goldman says the boom remains small relative to retail equity volumes and does not explain the decline in retail equity trading. Robinhood data show a near-doubling of retail options trading over the past year.

Goldman's Speculative Trading Indicator rolled over from its mid-2025 multi-decade high and now sits in the 80th percentile since 1995. Margin balances at big retail brokers remain very elevated but have not risen since June.

The $12T of equity in self-directed brokerage accounts is about 18% of total household equity assets (roughly $65T including direct and indirect holdings). Households own 42% of the US market directly and a majority including indirect ownership.

Households bought $840B of US equities in H1 2026 per Fed data. YTD inflows to US equity funds total $350B and remain robust in recent months. Trailing 4-quarter net household demand is near $1.5T (read off the chart).

The top 10% of households by wealth own 87% of household equity assets, the top 1% own 47%, and the bottom 50% own 1% (after Goldman strips out hedge funds the Fed includes in the household sector). Liquid wealth from large public offerings should remain a tailwind in coming quarters.

US public and private corporates issued a net $175B of equity in H1 2026 and corporate demand has dropped below zero. Including expiring lockups, Goldman expects net public equity supply next year to rise by the largest amount since 2000, so household demand will be crucial.

Paul Tudor Jones warned this month that the flow picture is the worst since 2002 and said he would be short all of 2027 (as reported by ZeroHedge). Goldman agrees on supply but argues households can absorb it.

Household equity allocation is a record 55% of financial assets and has tracked valuations closely for six decades. The only other time both were this high was 2000. Of the drivers of fund flows, the yield on cash has the largest negative effect.

Goldman's 2027 baseline assumes a stable labor market and modest declines in yields, which Snider says should be supportive. The 10Y is at 5.0% and Goldman sees it at 4.5% in 12 months. Labor market and interest rate paths are the key determinants of household demand, with AI-related disruption listed as a risk.

Structural support: 401(k) plans have grown from 13% of US retirement assets in 1995 to 21% today, and equity allocations in them have risen, including from 76% to 90% for participants in their twenties between 2013 and 2023.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Weak real income growth and elevated gasoline prices weigh on consumer sentiment and retail trading activity.
A high yield on cash and bonds competes with equities for household money, the largest negative driver of equity fund flows.
Modest yield declines are part of the baseline supporting household equity demand in 2027.
Households more than covered the net equity issuance in the first half.
Corporates have flipped from net buyers to net issuers, raising the supply households must absorb.

risk_factors: Net US public equity supply is expected to rise next year by the most since 2000 including expiring lockups.
Household demand depends on the labor market, interest rates, rising household net worth and open IPO windows.
Household equity allocation is a record 55% of financial assets, leaving less room for further buying.
The 10Y yield at 5.0% gives households a competing alternative to equities.
AI-related disruption is listed as a risk to household allocations.
Household equity ownership is concentrated in the top 10% of households (87% of assets), so demand relies on a narrow wealthy group.
Hedge fund crowding and short-term stop-driven selling could continue to cause disorderly unwinds.
vol_and_positioning: Goldman's Hedge Fund VIP long/short basket pair fell about 4% on Thursday, the worst one-day move since DeepSeek Monday (Jan 2025) and March 2020 on Snider's decade lookback, and the worst day since 2011 on the Prime desk's longer lookback.
Hedge funds degrossed in 7 of the past 8 sessions. Fundamental hedge fund net leverage is near 5-year lows while gross leverage is above the 90th percentile on a 5-year view.
90% of Prime book gross is in quants and multi-managers, so short-term stops matter more than medium-term value (Louis Miller).

Retail share of US equity volume is 9%, down from 15% late last year. Retail share of trading in leveraged ETFs is roughly double that in unlevered ETFs, and the 10 biggest levered products saw a surge of inflows over the past two weeks.
Goldman's Speculative Trading Indicator is in the 80th percentile since 1995 after a mid-2025 peak. Margin balances at big retail brokers are very elevated but flat since June.
Per ZeroHedge, hedge funds dumped AI stocks at a record pace a week earlier while retail bought with 3x leverage.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman: households bought $840B of US equities in H1 2026 and $350B flowed into US equity funds YTD. Its baseline of a stable labor market and modest yield declines keeps household demand solid in 2027, with 401(k) flows as a steady structural bid.
tension_points.bear_case: Net public equity supply is set to rise next year by the most since 2000 while corporate demand is below zero. Household equity allocation is a record 55%, the 10Y is at 5.0%, and Paul Tudor Jones warned the flow picture is the worst since 2002.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A deteriorating labor market or higher interest rates, which Goldman names as the key determinants of household equity demand.

theme_stances.key_argument: Household demand has stayed strong this year despite weaker retail trading and should remain solid in 2027, balancing rising equity supply.
theme_stances.evidence: Household demand will be crucial to balance this supply.

theme_stances.key_argument: A sharp hedge fund derisking underscores the importance of household demand for US equities.
theme_stances.evidence: A sharp hedge fund derisking this week and an ongoing increase in equity supply
